D8: Budget is unknown precisely but HURIDOCS has multiple major funders (Oak Foundation, Google, European Commission, etc.) suggesting a medium budget (likely £1–5M/yr range for a medium-sized Geneva NGO with 40+ years of operation), placing it at D3. scores.rater_notes: Martus is a genuinely significant human rights documentation tool operating since 2003 across ~50 countries, now discontinued as of May 2018. Not a 5 because it is primarily a documentation/evidence tool rather than one that challenges the fundamental mechanism of power reproduction. D2 scored 2: the tool primarily enables NGOs to collect and consult on abuses; it does not directly empower citizens to control outcomes, though it feeds into accountability processes. D3 scored 4: at the time of its peak operation, there was no comparable free, open-source, encrypted human rights documentation platform with this breadth of deployment; SecureDrop addresses a different use case. D4 scored 3: ~50 jurisdictions deployed but user numbers are not documented; conservatively estimated in the 10,000–100,000 range given grassroots NGO focus across 50 countries. D5 scored 2: open-source with an API/server architecture, but limited evidence of downstream projects building on it; primarily a standalone tool. D6 is listed in cannot_assess because while the dossier references academic citations and use in prosecutions, no specific verifiable accountability outcomes (named cases, policy changes) are documented — scored 3 conservatively based on the stated use for prosecutions and the breadth of deployment in conflict zones. D8 is listed in cannot_assess because exact budget figures are unknown; scored 4 based on the inference that a small Benetech team maintained this for 15 years on grants, achieving international deployment — resource efficiency appears high. The project's discontinuation in 2018 is a significant factor; its historical impact is real but ongoing impact is limited.
